current_disclosures.section: Products, Market, and Sales > Product Technologies
current_disclosures.summary: DRAM products are volatile, low-latency memory devices used in various markets including data centers, PCs, and automotive. In 2025, the company began shipping the industry's first 1γ production node incorporating EUV lithography for improved efficiency, while the majority of DRAM bit production remained on the 1ß node. This portfolio includes specialized types such as High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) for AI and high-performance computing, Double Data Rate (DDR) including DDR5, Low-Power DRAM (LPDDR) for mobile devices, and Graphics DRAM (GDDR) for graphics-intensive applications.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded Processor and GPU Product Portfolio

comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose high-performance graphics and compute capabilities, but AMD focuses on embedded CPUs, APUs, and GPUs for enterprise/automotive markets, whereas Micron focuses specifically on GDDR memory optimized for graphics processing units (GPUs). AMD highlights 3D graphics performance for automotive infotainment, while Micron highlights GDDR's high-bandwidth and data rates for gaming consoles and graphics cards.
